text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Since you are presenting with a limp and localized pain in your leg, could you tell me exactly where it hurts and what activity was happening when it started? You mentioned there is no fever, right?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Osgood-Schlatter Disease

This 7-year-old male presents with left knee pain and a limp, favoring the left leg during activity without fever or trauma. Given the age and typical presentation of anterior knee pain in the knee region during growth spurts, this is highly suggestive of Osgood-Schlatter disease. Please confirm if the pain is specifically located at the tibial tuberosity and if it worsens with running or jumping.
